name: Qwen-Coder (latest large, e.g., Qwen3-Coder-MoE)
description: Qwen-Coder latest large is the Qwen code-specialist path for production code generation, agentic coding, and refactoring workloads, with the current official family collection showing 480B and 31B-class releases rather than a single small dense checkpoint. The deployment implication is that this variant sits at the high-capacity end of the Qwen code stack, so it is best used where quality and tool-use reliability justify very large serving footprints and more complex infrastructure. For self-hosted production, the practical trade-off is favorable memory and deployment simplicity versus lower capacity headroom for the hardest reasoning and long-context jobs.

best_for: Code generation and autocomplete at high quality thresholds.
Agentic coding workflows that require large context and tool-use reliability.
Refactoring and repository-scale code transformation tasks.
avoid_for: Small single-GPU deployments with tight VRAM budgets.
Simple code completion tasks that do not justify the serving footprint.
Latency-sensitive edge inference where smaller Qwen3 or Qwen3-Coder siblings are sufficient.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Large-scale production coding assistants and agentic developer tooling where the model can be served on high-memory GPU infrastructure.
deployment_risks: Assuming the latest large code model can be deployed like a small dense model without multi-GPU planning.
failure_modes: Code-edit correctness and tool-call instability under aggressive quantization.
OOM or latency spikes during long-context repository-scale queries.
common_mistakes: Sizing memory based on average prompt length rather than the maximum realistic repository prompt for 262K context.
Treating quantized builds as drop-in replacements without validating patch correctness and tool-use behavior.
operational_notes: The official cloud model cards expose a 262,144-token context length and 65,536-token max output, which materially changes KV-cache sizing and request admission policy compared with smaller coding models.

The large code-specialist line is intended for advanced software development tasks, so serving should preserve long-context capacity for repository-level prompts rather than aggressively truncating inputs.
For production, throughput-oriented engines such as vLLM are the most practical path when you need batching and concurrent code-agent requests.

The official Qwen3-Coder collection currently surfaces multiple large releases, which means variant pinning matters more than family-level selection if you need reproducible behavior across environments.
Managed-service deployment via Google Cloud’s model cards is the cleanest path if you want the official 262K/65K limits without owning the full serving stack.
Self-hosted deployment should assume multi-GPU planning for the largest releases rather than trying to size them like small dense models.
Keep prompt budgets large enough to preserve repository context; the official context window is one of the main reasons to choose this class.
Use quantization only after evaluating correctness on code-edit tasks, because code models are often more sensitive to quantization-induced regressions than chat models.
Route short completion requests to smaller siblings if you need to protect capacity for long-context agentic jobs.
vLLM is the clearest verified self-hosting target among open runtimes in the reviewed material.
Variant differentiation (Identity): the official Qwen3-Coder collection includes 480B and 31B-class model entries.
Variant differentiation (Specifications): 262,144 for the official cloud-hosted Qwen3-Coder GA model card surfaced by Google Cloud/Vertex AI and Gemini Enterprise docs.
Variant differentiation (File Formats): GGUF is not officially documented for the latest official Qwen-VL variant in the reviewed sources.

Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): this is the most deployable Qwen3 MoE checkpoint for cost-sensitive production, and hardware planning is mostly about whether you want quantized single-GPU service or BF16 multi-GPU service.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): use the Hugging Face model card for checkpoint-specific serving notes and the Qwen download portal for canonical distribution paths and quantized artifacts.

Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): the runtime story is strongest for vLLM and SGLang because the official docs expose reasoning-mode controls directly, which matters for this instruct checkpoint’s behavior contract.

Variant differentiation (Deployment): the 30B-A3B instruct checkpoint is the best fit when you need reasoning-quality MoE behavior but want a materially smaller active-parameter budget than the flagship model.
Variant differentiation (License): license terms do not materially distinguish this variant from the rest of the family; deployment economics are the differentiator.
Variant differentiation (Status): this checkpoint is released as an active production model, not a research-only artifact, and remains part of the current Qwen3 deployment stack.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-1.7B): Smaller dense sibling for lightweight local inference.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-4B): Mid-size dense sibling with lower serving cost.
Variant relationship (qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct-maas): Managed-service deployment target for the largest official Qwen3-Coder release.
